passage:
Dear Francis,
You asked why I've gone quiet for two weeks. Ma's cousin, Bablu Mama, arrived 'for two days' to see a doctor in Kolkata. That was eleven days ago. I smile, I give up my bed, I sleep on the sitting-room divan, and every morning I wonder: how long? Ma cooks three meals a day for him and says nothing, because in our house you never ask a guest when he's leaving.
Yesterday I finally sat with him over tea and said, 'Mama, my exams start Monday. Could we plan your dates so I have my room back by then?' He laughed, embarrassed, and said Saturday. Then he offered to take Ma to the market. Maybe asking was kinder than sulking.
Anirban

qa.q: How long has Bablu Mama been staying?
What has Anirban been feeling while sleeping on the divan each night?
qa.a: Anirban has felt tired and quietly resentful, smiling on the outside while wondering how long the stay would last.

qa.q: What made Anirban's talk with Bablu Mama work?
qa.a: Anirban spoke privately over tea, gave a real reason and asked to plan the dates together, which was honest without being rude.

qa.q: How might Bablu Mama have felt when Anirban raised the dates?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed at first, but perhaps also relieved to have a plan, and he answered by offering to help Ma.

grounding: Shows a host who smiles while wondering how long a relative will stay, and finds that a gentle, honest talk about timing protects both hospitality and the relationship.

passage: 'You know my cousin Dorjee, from Kalimpong?' Tenzin asks Maria as they walk to class. 'He dropped in three Sundays ago. No call, just a bag and a big smile. Our rule at home is, a guest is a guest. So I rolled out my mattress, cooked thukpa, lent him my laptop. Every night I lay awake thinking, is it one more week? Two? I couldn't just ask. It felt so rude. Then Ama-la did something clever. At dinner she asked him, very sweetly, "Dorjee, when does your college term start? We want to pack you some dried cheese." He told us: Thursday. Nobody was hurt, and I finally slept.'

qa.q: What did Tenzin cook for Dorjee?
What was Tenzin feeling while lying awake each night?
qa.a: Tenzin felt anxious and stuck, wanting to know how long Dorjee would stay but worried that asking would seem rude.

qa.q: Why did Ama-la's question work well?
qa.a: It asked about timing warmly and came with a kind offer, so Dorjee could share his plans without feeling pushed out.

qa.q: How might Dorjee have felt when asked about his college term?
qa.a: Dorjee probably felt cared for rather than unwelcome, since the question came with an offer of food for the journey.

grounding: Illustrates a host who keeps smiling while privately wondering how long an unannounced relative will stay, and a gentle question about timing that protects both hospitality and the relationship.
